questions.text: Which statement best describes growth?
options: Cells becoming specialized for different jobs
An irreversible increase in size, weight, or cell count
Gaining new abilities such as flying

questions.text: Which is an example of development rather than growth?
options: A baby gaining 1 kg in weight
Stem cells turning into muscle, brain, or skin cells

questions.text: How is growth usually measured?
options: With scales, tape measures, or rulers
By watching which genes switch on
By counting functional milestones like walking

questions.text: In plants, growth is mostly restricted to the...
options: meristems at the root and shoot tips, and the cambium

questions.text: Which life process is 'getting rid of body waste'?
Where does human fertilization take place?
What is a zygote?
options: A hollow ball of about 100 cells
An embryo with three germ layers
The 1-cell stage formed when a sperm fertilizes an egg

questions.text: During cleavage, the embryo...
options: divides rapidly inside the egg shell without getting bigger overall

questions.text: Which stage is a solid, berry-like ball of about 16 cells on Day 3?
Which part of the blastocyst becomes the baby?
Which germ layer builds the skin, hair, eyes, and the entire nervous system?
Which germ layer builds muscles, bones, the heart, and the kidneys?
Which germ layer forms the lining of the stomach and intestines, the liver, pancreas, and lungs?
Which protective bag fills with watery fluid to cushion the baby from bumps?
Which structure forms the baby's side of the placenta?
After birth, human growth follows what kind of curve?
options: A flat curve with no change

questions.text: During which stage do children grow steadily at about 5 cm per year?
Why do young children rarely break bones when they fall?
options: Their bones are already completely solid
Their muscles are stronger than adults'
Their bones start out as flexible cartilage and harden slowly

questions.text: Growth in adulthood stops when the epiphyseal plates...
Which hormone from the testes helps drive puberty in boys?
What is menarche?
options: The first menstrual cycle in girls

questions.text: What is metamorphosis?
options: A big change in shape and body structure as a young animal becomes an adult
A small increase in body weight
The division of a zygote into many cells

questions.text: Which butterfly stage hangs upside down in a silk cocoon while its body rebuilds?
How does a young tadpole breathe?
What happens to a froglet's tail as it becomes an adult frog?
options: It shrinks away and is used as food

questions.text: Ferns and mosses reproduce using...
What is the tiny heart-shaped gametophyte of a fern called?
Why do ferns and mosses need rain or dew for fertilization?
options: So the spores can be eaten
So the sperm can swim to the egg

questions.text: In double fertilization, what does the second fusion produce?
What is the first step of seed germination?
options: Imbibition: the seed drinks water and swells until the seed coat cracks

questions.text: Which part of the embryo emerges first and grows down into the soil?
In phototropism, where does auxin move when light hits the stem from one side?
options: To the lit side of the stem
To the shaded side of the stem

questions.text: What does etiolation (growing in darkness) show?
options: Plants only grow in the dark
A plant can get taller (growth) without developing healthy tissues (development)
Growth and development are exactly the same
